And after everything, count yourself an unprofitable servant who has not been able to do what you ought. Say to yourself: "I am a hired labourer: why am I idle instead of finishing my work? I have been invited: why do I lag behind my companions? I have a great debt: when will I pay it? My journey is long: when will I complete my road, and how many provisions will suffice for it? My Lord has sent for me and is looking for me: when will I reach him? I am required to hasten: why do I carry the burden of earthly things and am bound with the fetters of love for the world? My companions keep vigil, and I sleep; my companions offer sacrifice, and I sin; my companions weep, and I laugh; my companions are afflicted, and I rejoice; my companions are silent, and I chatter; my companions meditate on their Lord, his kingdom and his glory, and I meditate on the things from which I was saved and from which I went out." And when you are about to grow weary during the night vigil, and your body grows heavy upon you, consider all these things and bring

to mind how many are standing on their feet; how many are bowed down; how many are on their knees; how many are lying on the ground; how many have found rest from the burden of the body; how many are drunk with the love of God and have forgotten their nature; how many are singing psalms in their hearts to the Lord. Then the meditation on these things will lift all heaviness and weariness from you, and you will offer fervent prayer many times over. And remember also how many are at this very moment awake over their worldly affairs: travellers on the road, ploughmen, craftsmen, shepherds, those keeping the night watch, those taking care of their own concerns, those guarding their masters. And if these toil so much for transitory things, how much more am I indebted to my Lord! When you stand for prayer, do not begin hastily, and do not perform your whole prayer slackly and wearily. But when you stand, sign yourself with the cross, gather your thoughts, prepare and make yourself ready, look to him to whom you are praying, and then begin. Compel yourself at the beginning of your prayer so that tears flow and there is compunction, and your whole prayer will be profitable. And when you see thoughts that hinder you, you need not leave a pause between one section of the psalter and the next. But if a confusion of thoughts persists against you, multiply prayers and tears more than the recitation of psalms, and drive them from you in every way you can, whether by changing the words or by some other means. Understand what I am saying. And again, if a profitable meditation comes to you, let it take the place of the psalm for you, and do not push away from you the gift of God in order to keep your rule. A prayer in which neither the meditation of God nor the fear of the mind is mingled is a labour of the flesh. Do not rejoice in a multitude of psalms while sloth lies upon your heart. Better one word spoken close at hand than a thousand from afar. At the time of prayer be [humble], simple, broken, pure of mind, and behold, you will see the glory of God. Put away from you all crafty and evil thoughts, and make yourself like a weaned child upon its mother, and blessed are you. And if the battle presses hard upon you in prayer, say your words: present your complaint, weep over your case, return answer to your [adversary] in anger until he is defeated. And your Lord, who sees your vigilance, will judge your cause with justice and condemn your enemy, and he will be found no more; and [?] your weakness. But if the passions of nature wage war against you, seek

relief from them from your Lord. And if unclean thoughts rise up in you, do not be distressed; only do not give in to them, nor receive them, nor give them room in your mind, and at once they will move on and pass away, like a traveller who turns aside to lodge for the night and leaves at dawn. Take care that your mind does not wander during the time of prayer in idle musing, so that instead of reconciliation you stir to anger the Judge whom you have offended. Before human judges there is fear, yet before God contempt! How can someone who does not perceive where he stands, and does not know what he is saying, suppose that he is offering his prayer? [One should be] awake in mind with compunction, standing on his feet, idle from sleep, turned away from the affairs of the world, [?] more than many, forgetting all these things, and [?] from the meditation of things that are not near to them and bring him no profit, just as dreams do not benefit those who see them. Rouse yourself: your Lord is speaking with you, do not wander; his chosen angels surround you, do not be dull; the ranks of the demons stand against you, do not grow slack. Know, then, my brother, that just as the holy angels rejoice when they praise God, so in like manner the demons are distressed when they see us attending to prayer. For since they themselves were deprived of praising their Lord, they strive to keep us too from glorifying God, because they know that by it their schemes are brought to nothing, and that it is armour and shields against them; and they hurry to hinder us from glorifying. And when they see that we do not listen to them, and are constantly steadfast in our occupation, they contrive to harm us with thoughts and worldly memories. They snatch away our mind and paint before us shapes and likenesses, and the faces of people and conversation with them, sometimes of friends and sometimes of enemies, so that instead of the love of God we have the love of men, and instead of praying for our enemies, as we are commanded, we acquire hatred toward those who have distressed us, so that our prayer becomes a cause of anger. Beware, then, of their ambushes, and guard yourself from those who are ready in their wickedness, deceivers and deceived. Begin to travel the way of prayer constantly, and do not turn aside to the right or to the left, and you will quickly reach the dwelling-place of peace, [free] from dread and fear. And when your mind is accustomed and at rest, [offer] the offering of your prayer like Abel, and the one who stands against you will be put to shame. Be fearful before him at the time of prayer, and the words of your mouth will accord with the will of God. Again, of Mar Abraham the teacher.

And [?] concerning [repentance?]. At all times be mindful of your salvation, so that you do not grow weary. Look to your goal, so that you do not come to regret. Be discerning about your way of life, what it is, so that you are not like one who beats the air. You have yoked yourself to the yoke of patience: do not kick against it. You have made a vow: do not lie. You have begun: do not turn back and become a laughingstock. You have tasted that the Lord is good to those who wait for him and to the soul that seeks him: do not flee from toil. You have longed to share in the glory given to those who love him: do not exchange it for vanities. You have gone down into the contest: be strong in it. You have longed for the fair crown: strive hard until the day of your death. You have been thrown into battle: do not flee and take an arrow in your back like a coward. If the spirit of the ruler rises against you, do not leave your place. You have crucified your flesh with the passions and desires of the world: let your spirit not be grieved by afflictions, do not give way before temptations, do not be troubled by insults [?], do not be angry with your enemy, and do not judge your companion and despise him. For you were not made a disciple for this, but in this you are tested. [Beware] lest you condemn yourself and be judged by comparison with others. [Beware] lest, compared with your patience in former times, your endurance be found wanting [?], and compared with your zeal, your negligence be condemned, and you become your own accuser. Many began on the way of righteousness, but because their foundations were not laid upon the rock, when the winds of wickedness blew upon them and the rivers of floods and afflictions came, they fell at once, and great was their fall. And when labours pressed hard upon them, they gave up and changed course, like a hired labourer who, when the heat overtook him, fled from the work and was left without wages; like a building that has no roof, and like a weaving that is never finished. This, then, is how you can endure: by lightening the [burden] of your labours through looking to your reward, to the end of your life, which is near, and to the remembrance of the fearful judgement of Gehenna, and of how great a debt you owe. And bring to mind that, like sowers and like reapers, we are [near] to it [?], and that the time will come for us to reap, if we do not grow weary. Consider these things, and do not spare yourself labours, lest the blow of your enemy gain mastery over you. Toil is armour and shields in the battle against the evil one. The Lord has mercy on those who toil, and [?]

those who toil he gives rest in his kingdom; they rejoice in the success of their righteousness and delight in the just reward of their labours. But the slothful are wrapped in shame, and when they behold the grace [given to others], they are confounded. For labours win great boldness and confidence before Christ. And he loves those who are crushed for his name's sake, and reveals himself to them. God does not reject a broken heart, but accepts their repentance and causes them to dwell in joy. For the drops of sweat of these labours are a medicine of life. O my lord, repentance for God's sake makes us children of the kingdom, keeps us from sins, separates us from the evil one, gives us health of soul, and makes us worthy of open boldness before Christ. An admonition to the brothers by the holy Mar Abraham. Show the death of the world visibly [?] in your way of life, and portray the image of the kingdom in your person, [?] it through the virtues that befit the banquet. Bear in your conduct the burden of exile, and toil always on the way of truth. Bear patiently [?] the hunger of abstinence, and glean ears of grain in affliction, like your Lord. Bear the insults of the insolent and give thanks, and do not be distressed; offer up thanksgiving, for it is to your profit. Bear your pains with joy, for your sufferings are your [reward?]. And rejoice every hour in your mind that your sufferings pass away and you live. Bear visibly on your shoulder the cross that became your victory; leave the city of the dead and go to the land of the luminous ones. Bear the crucifixion of your members, quench the desire of your mind, give perfection to repentance, and justice will not be exacted of you [?]. Bear purity like Moses, and cleanse your heart of iniquity; and the light that shone forth from the Father will clothe your senses together with your movements. Bear truth within your heart, and show its rays in your members; and the fire that consumed the Chaldeans will become a chariot for your mind. Bear the compunction of humility and [ask for] the forgiveness of debts in prayer; and the tears that [?] in the apple of your eye will [quench] the fire of [torment?] [?]. Bear love like [?], and know the Just One in your purity; and the hand that [reached out to?] [?] will hold you fast so that you do not sink. Bear zeal like Elijah, and rebuke the blemishes of sinners; and the hosts that were [with Elisha?] [?] will accompany you all your days. Bear submission to your superiors, and honour them while giving thanks; and the Spirit that clothed Elisha will [come]

to you, and you will live. Bear stillness [?] like David, and slay with the [swords?] of grace; and the strength that strengthened the mighty man will sustain you in the time of afflictions. Bear serenity of thoughts; [?] to have pity on sinners; and the mercies that are gracious to sinners will release you from your debts. Bear your reproaches with joy, and pray for whoever is hostile to you [?]; and the [?] that helped the apostles will rest in you fully [?]. Again, counsels of admonition to the sisters, by Mar Abraham. Purify your heart and humble your thoughts. And even if you have stripped off sin, do not boast too much before your departure. Purify your mind of evil meditation, and if you are wronged while innocent, remember that it was a human being who distressed you. Purify your heart of the meditation of envy, and when you see your brother who has hurt you, be reconciled before him [?]. Purify your heart of the [?] of mammon, and pray every hour that your life may be emptied of its bitter roots. Purify your heart of the love of luxuries, so that you do not give room to the passions, and harsh [desires?] do not make sport of you. Purify your heart of anger, so that bitterness does not gain mastery over you, and the demon who delights in confusion does not cast you continually into affliction. Purify your thought of the [heat?] of the burning coal, so that your desire is not fettered by it and does not fill your path with stumbling blocks. Humble your inner self, [keeping it] from the cliffs of vainglory, lest you fall before your enemies and your adversary gloat over you. Turn your eyes away from the desire for the flesh of women, so that you do not grind at the mill like Samson, and the light of your lamp be darkened. Rouse yourself, so that the world does not swallow you; for it shows no mercy to whoever falls into its hands. Learn to conquer your passions, so that they do not enslave you; for if they overcome you, your life will be [full of] distress [?]. Fight against sleep, so that [heaviness?] may be driven far from you; but if you are overcome by it, you are deprived of spiritual vision. Do not boast if you have gone out from the body [?], for this is a work of grace. And you, how much remains for you to complete [?]. Remember that you are a human being: when desire enslaves you, stretch out your mind toward the Hidden One [?] and ask help from him. And do not love praise, so that the Lord may bring you near to his glory. Walk in the way of abstinence, so that your mind is not troubled; and from whoever is [diligent] in repentance, take remedies for yourself. Guard your tongue from deceit and your desire from vainglory. And where humility dwells, ask for the help of prayer. Rest in stillness is its way, and its teaching [?]. And if [?] raises [?]

in love, it escapes from fear. Do not long for the outward show of this age, for time is short [?]. Hire yourself out for that delight which no end overtakes. Do not live with someone envious and grasping, who has no mercy, for closeness to him separates you from God. Surrender your body to him who gave you his body, and hand yourself over to him who handed himself over for our redemption. Let the world go; let it depart from you, for you know that it passes away from you. What does not remain with you — why should your concern go after it? Give praise at all times and do not grow weary. Go out from the old man through love of what is to come; and once you have put on [the new] by grace, do not fear justice. Do not mix any blemish into your truth, nor dispute into your faith; for the Maker is not to be searched out — only let praise be offered up to him. Do not remain a child to the end; rather, the word you speak, fulfil it first in deed. For if your word is true but your conduct is lame, who would see it and not weep that you have loved darkness more than light? Let not your bodily affection [hold you back?] even as far as [?] abstinence; for you have heard that it returns to dust. Let it weep and shed tears up to the grave. Let your inner love wail with groans, so that you too may be delivered by the Lord [?] on the day of awakening from wrath. Do not let your mind waver in time of temptation; for gold is tested in fire, and the penitent in the furnace of afflictions. The craftsman, however, takes great pains over its form, so that it is not spoiled in its [?]. Counsels and instructions with admonition, likewise by Mar Abraham. Truth is a great pillar; it is a light in which there is no darkness. Before all your deeds, acquire truth; and before all your works, acquire faith. For every person who does all his deeds in truth, his deeds have a good end; and whoever performs his works in faith, faith gives him a hand toward all holy works. If someone says to you, "You have truth with me," yet he does not have the truth of deeds, he is a liar and there is no truth in him. And if someone tells you that a person who eats and drinks his fill, wears fine clothes, does the will of desire, and lives with women who serve him, keeps holiness, he is a liar: do not believe him. For every person

who throws himself into the eating of meat and the drinking of wine is a servant of fornication. As Scripture also testifies, saying: "Whoever sows in his body will reap corruption from his body." For there is nothing sown that does not sprout, nothing conceived that is not born, nothing planted that does not come up, nothing hidden that is not revealed, and nothing concealed that is not made known. All the hidden things of a person come to light, and all the secrets of men come to be revealed, and all their concealed deeds are laid out before all the generations [?]. The wicked are put to shame by the works of their iniquity, and the righteous rejoice in the works of their righteousness. For just as these bodily works that are seen to be wicked corrupt this body, which is visible, so also these hidden evils that are not seen corrupt the soul, which is not visible. And if someone tells you that whoever lives with his father and his mother, acquires gold, and busies himself with the cares of the world, with the building of houses [?] and with the delusion of empty wealth is a disciple of Christ, it is plain that you must not believe him. If you do believe him, you make the words of Christ a lie, for he said: "Whoever does not part from all that he has cannot be my disciple." And of the one who does not leave his father and his mother, his brothers and his sisters, and take up his cross and come after me, he said: "He is not worthy of me." For no one can be a disciple of Christ unless he has trained in his contest [?], learned his craft, taken up his cross, shared in his sufferings, and entered into the order of his death. So everyone who possesses this world is a disciple of the world, and everyone who parts from this world is a disciple of Christ. Therefore, if the name of Christianity is called upon you, conduct yourself in the way that befits you [?], and labor for the sake of your name, so that you do not belittle Christianity by your deeds. And if the name of virginity and holiness is called upon you, do deeds that befit your name, and do not belittle the name of virginity by your evil conduct. And if you are a son of the covenant, keep your covenant with the beautiful name [?]; the covenant you keep will keep you. If you are not careful with yourself, you will fall from

your covenant, and the Gehenna of fire will receive you. Therefore, if you wish to keep true holiness, put on the armor of fasting, be strengthened by humility, grow strong in endurance, torment your soul with hunger, afflict your body with thirst, and dry up the veins of your blood. For in a body that is pure and lean, holiness shines, and in wasted flesh the joy of purity flourishes; but in a body that is moist and fat, the fire of fornication burns. Therefore, if you are striving for the crown of holiness, you must go down into the contest, struggle against the desire of your body and the hearing of your ears, win the contest within and the battle without, and fight against the sight of the day and the sleep of the night. For there is no crown without a contest, no victory without battle, no prize without a race, no wage without work, no rest without toil, no comfort without mourning, and no relief without affliction. For whoever leaves this world for the sake of Christ goes and inherits the world to come, which has been promised to the saints. Whoever leaves the kingdom of the earth goes and inherits the heavenly kingdom. Whoever leaves a father according to the flesh goes and becomes a son of the Father who is in heaven. Whoever leaves a mother according to the flesh goes and becomes a son of the Holy Spirit. Whoever leaves brothers and sisters goes and becomes a brother of Christ. Whoever leaves an earthly table goes and delights at the table of the kingdom. Whoever leaves an earthly garden enters the garden of light. Whoever leaves earthly wealth acquires heavenly wealth. Whoever leaves his city and his village goes and inherits the Jerusalem that is in heaven. So everyone who leaves possessions that die, buildings that fall, garments that wear out, beauty that fades, glory that passes, pleasure that ceases, youth that turns to old age, and joy that changes into sorrow, goes and receives in their place, in the world that does not pass away, rest that does not cease, satisfaction that does not end, beauty that does not fade, youth that does not grow old, childhood that does not change, a garment of glory and a crown of light, a robe of honor and a diadem of kingship, which neither pass away nor are dissolved for ever. But if you wish to win in the contest of holiness and be crowned with the crown of virginity, let your whole battle be against your soul

and your whole struggle against the desire of your body. Hold your soul back from its demands and deprive it of its desires. Do not follow its counsels, do not listen to its agitations [?], do not follow its persuasions, do not believe its enticements, and do not let it lead you astray with its many words. For it speaks and does not act; it promises and does not fulfill; it swears and does not keep its oath; it makes covenants and breaks them. It keeps you hanging on an empty hope and crowns you with an idle expectation. It shrinks from fasting and wearies of vigils; it despises long prayers; it is deceitful and takes refuge in the pains and illnesses of the body. It runs from spiritual labor and takes refuge in bodily works. It fears seclusion and flees from the recollection of the mind. It loves distraction and amusement and the wandering of evil thoughts. It clings to fancies [?] and flies about in the air. It abandons the divine knowledge that would lift it to the lofty height of heaven and clings to evil impulses that sink it into the depths below. It runs from what would raise it on high and goes after what casts it down into the lower depths. It fears instruction and flees from discipline. It hates those who rebuke it and loves those who praise it. It flees from the chaste and clings to the frivolous. It hates silence and loves the distraction of idle words. It runs from hearing the words of God and longs to hear the tales of the world. When it hears the words of the holy Scriptures, it is bored and dozes off; but when it hears words of amusement, it is wide awake and glad. When it rises for the vigil, its strength fails and the light of its eyes goes out [?]; but when it goes off to work, its mind wakes up and grows strong. Faced with fasting, its face darkens. It hates spiritual delight and loves bodily delight. It fears the spiritual labor that enriches it, and loves the bodily comforts that impoverish it. It is awake for bodily things that kill it and asleep to spiritual things that give it life. When you give it rest, it is not satisfied; and when you yield to its desires, it never says, "Enough." When you have held it back from many desires, it asks you for small ones; and when you have given it the small ones, it asks you for great ones. And when you have relieved it of afflictions, it soon asks you for desires. The more you slacken it, the further down it goes; and when you hold on to it,

it rises upward. Upward, the bond of the subtle mind draws it to ascend; and downward, the desire of the body hangs on it so that it descends. For the things of the body come very easily to it, and the things of the Spirit are very hard for it [?]. This is the nature of the soul with which we are clothed. Therefore do not listen to it; even if it does not stir you up, do not trust it; even if it does not lead you astray. For many are its sayings and its explanations. With bodily things it hurries you to have them quickly; with spiritual things it keeps you hanging on an empty hope. As for food, drink, sleep and rest, it urges you to have them at once in practice; but as for vigil, fasting and prayer, it promises them for later and does not do them. Everyone who agrees with it, it makes a liar; and whoever believes it in all it tells him, it disgraces [?] and leaves empty and lacking in all the works of the fear of God and of righteousness. Fight a second battle as well, against your body. Bind it with seclusion, fetter it with fasting, hang it on a cross, and take its weapons from it, which are food, drink, sleep and rest. Afflict it with hunger, drive it with thirst, crucify it with vigil, wear it out with toil, and exhaust it with weariness. Let it grow weak in its hunger, its thirst, its labor and its weariness, and its war against you will cease. For it is better for you that it should be thinking about bread than thinking about sin; and it is better for you that in its thirst it should be seeking water than seeking uncleanness. For if you give your body rest, it oppresses you; if you honor it, it dishonors you; if you pamper it, it torments you; and if you loose it from its bonds, it binds us with evil desires. For it is a master of rebels, and it constantly demands its comforts. By day it demands its food and drink, and by night its bed and its rest. With the business of its food, its drink, its sleep and its rest we are occupied night and day, and it does not let us serve God. The whole world is under the yoke of the body and serves it as a slave. For its sake the earth is worked; for its sake people travel the seas. Sowing and reaping are for its sake; fruits and stones [?] for its sake; wild beasts and cattle for its sake; birds and fish for its sake. For its sake people make war on one another, to satisfy the desires of the body. For its sake come robberies and oppressions; for its sake murder and adultery

are committed among people. And it is not enough for it that the whole world serves it as a slave; it even wishes to enslave in its works the chosen ones of God, those who have left the world behind them, who have despised the desires of the earth, who have [withdrawn?] from the table of the body, and renounced the foods of their delights and all its empty glory, its vain care and its comfort. It wishes to keep them from the work of God and to trouble them so that they do not do the works of righteousness. But those who know its devices despise its pleasures and beware of its snares, and they serve God in truth. Therefore run so that you may reach the goal; seek so that you may find; struggle so that you may win; fight so that you may save your soul; contend in the contest so that you may receive the crown. For the fighter who opposes you is strong in his might and armed with every kind of weapon. If you slacken, he throws you down; if you are negligent, he defeats you. If you feed him, he grows strong against you and conquers you; and if you make him great, he overthrows you. But if you rouse your spirit and strengthen your mind, you defeat him and rule over him, and the Holy Power strengthens you. If you take refuge in God, he becomes your Savior; and when you trust in him with all your heart and all your strength and believe in him, he in his mercies helps you in all you call on him for. To him be glory and honor and thanksgiving and worship from the mouths of all rational beings for ever and ever. Amen.

By Mar Abraham. Encouragement and warning, with admonition, to the solitary brothers.

Do not be grieved when the sufferings of nature come upon you, for these are the ways of the body, and they happen. And never again stand in despair when you fall into sins, for you have the medicine of repentance, and repentance heals what is lacking. Let not the Adversary bring you low through his warfare, for even if he knocks [?], we do not open the door to him. For great is the passion of the high priest of our confession, by the standard of whose victory all the devices of the Evil One are brought to nothing. Do not be cast down in your mind when nature demands what it needs. It is a small thing [?] that fills you, and it does not leave you idle [?]. In every affliction that befalls you, cast yourself before God and be comforted. For our Creator does not rejoice that the sinner should perish. Do not lower your gaze from on high, and let not the thought of the Judge be forgotten

from your heart. Always look toward [?] and toward the recompense of our deeds. Do not abandon the holy reading [to which you were called?], nor the good teaching you have learned. Be strengthened by the hope of the promises and fortified by the recompense of deeds. Beware of the fire of torment, and flee from the weeping of Gehenna. Remember that you are a son of God, a brother of the Father's Beloved, a member of the company of the apostles, a sharer in the portion of the martyrs, a guest at the table of the confessors, an heir with the saints, a partaker in the support of the prophets, in the delight of the righteous, in the praises of the angels, in the response of the cherubim and the seat of the seraphim, a sharer in the portion of the Lord Christ, one invited to the wedding feast of the Only-begotten, a member of the camps of the heavenly hosts, and a dweller in the Jerusalem above. When you bring these things to mind, you do not fall into the works of darkness; you are strengthened in your repentance, and unclean thoughts do not choke you. Consider to what you have been called, and see that empty [?] does not wear you down. Do not look to those who are wise according to the flesh, who are older than you in years; look to the young who are older than you in the fear of the Spirit, and catch up with them. Do not incline your ear to hear the words of the frivolous [?], the tales of the shameless, or the teaching of [?]. Draw near to the books of [?], and bind up your pains with purity of soul. Why does your life slip away without victories for God? Meditate every hour with groaning, so that repentance may dawn in your heart. The measure of love is truth, and the knowledge of faith is a treasure [?]. A soul from which these things are far, why has it put on Christ? It is voices for the ears and words for the hearing. And if the remembrance of good conduct is far from it, it is a house built on sand. A soul that keeps remembrance discerns the ways of humility; but a heart empty of love is seed that fell on rock. The fear of God does not dwell in a person who chases after every wind, and in whom love of the belly prevails. Because he is divided over his life, he is trampled by his belly in every [?] toward everyone.

Further, to the brothers who love humility. By Mar Abraham.

Love of this world angers God, distracts the mind and leads the sight astray. Despise the desires of the flesh, so that the fire of nature [?] does not seize you. Bend your belly with hunger and thirst, so that the covenant of our Lord is not forgotten from your heart. Pray at all times, so that you do not fall into the hand of the Adversary. Despise the beauty of luxuries,

so that the fire of greed does not seize you. Sprinkle [?] your soul with afflictions, so that the right hand of the Most High may hover over you. Shed tears of groaning before the Judge, so that he may blot out the bond of your debts. Let go of the joy of this time and of bodily comforts, so that you may be found worthy of the knowledge of the saints. Recite without ceasing [?] the psalms of the son of Jesse, so that evil demons may be driven far from you. Entrust your life in this time to the hand of your Creator, so that the works of darkness may be driven away from you. Become poor in the treasures of this transient world, so that you may delight at the table of Lazarus. Sacrifice yourself to the one who sacrificed himself for you, so that you may recline on his bosom at supper on the last day. Meditate on the books of virtue, so that you may come to the dwelling [?] by the narrow way that leads to the kingdom. Hate the things that death makes pass away, and trade in the treasures that are kept in heaven. Despise praise and do not fear reproach, for in these things you are dead to the world. Do not be troubled. Lower your gaze from the precious things of the world, so that your rest does not become your ruin. Pharaoh, who was false toward God [?], the world made unpersuadable. Therefore at all times marvel [?] at the fear of the Trinity, so that thoughts of burning [?] may flee from before you. Betroth your soul to the Bridegroom, so that he may bring you in to the wedding of the Beloved. Turn away from the door of revelry [?], so that the door of the pit [?] is not opened against you. Stop your ears from hearing gossip about a matter unseen, so that your tongue does not become a spring of hateful things. Keep far from the company of the noble [?], and see who is humble, and trust him. Do not think that you are wise; rather be one who learns and does, not one who teaches [?]. Then this will be counted to you as a man of God [?]. Humble yourself so that you may be exalted. Become poor so that you may become rich. Hunger so that you may be satisfied. Thirst so that you may be refreshed. Be despised so that you may be honored. Suffer so that you may be glorified. Be persecuted so that you may find rest. Strip yourself so that you may be clothed. Weep so that you may rejoice [?]. Die so that you may live. Keep vigil so that you may shine. Fast so that you may exult. Mourn so that you may be gladdened. Pray so that you may be saved. Repent so that you may receive mercy. Seek so that you may find. Knock so that it may be opened to you. Run so that you may reach the goal. Labor so that you may inherit. Give so that it may be given to you. Show mercy so that mercy may be shown to you. Carry your cross so that you may glory in light. Subdue [?] your body and harden your limbs. Hate mammon and flee from high places. Despise boasting and put on a spirit of humility. Leave the passions of women, and be in virginity

worthy of praise. Let go of the purse of mammon, and stretch out your hand in generosity of spirit to almsgiving. Weep over your soul with groans, so that you do not ask for mercy in the court of judgment and receive no answer. Be bowed and constrained in your will, so that you do not thirst like the rich man to whom Lazarus did not [give?]. Let your soul be despicable in your eyes, so that in spirit you may live on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ. You are the image of the One who is exalted above the world. Be diligent in good deeds, so that you do not become like the poor [?] copy of a painter unskilled in his craft, which is rejected because the likeness he made does not resemble the original. But you are the likeness of the Painter of all beauty. Adorn yourself with the colors of the virtues, so that the Painter does not loathe you because of you [?], and the beauty of your form is not ruined. Bear the likeness of your Creator in the deeds of your works, and show the beauty of the [image of the?] Hidden One in the purity of your thoughts. Reveal the Hidden One by your wisdom, and make his power known by your truthfulness. Begin [?] on [?] with your tears, and proclaim the promises by your endurance. Rebuke [?] the frivolous by your silence, and shame the dissolute by your fasting. Rouse the sleepers by your vigil, and encourage sinners by your appearance. Shame the greedy by your frugality [?], and reprove the rich by your [poverty?]. Be a stranger to the world, and reveal the power of love. Pluck anger out of your heart, and blend your soul with repentance. Restrain your tongue from murmuring, and let it sing praise to the Hidden One. Strip your dwelling of gold, so that the Spirit of the Lord may dwell in you. Rule over your belly, so that the snares of deceit may be cut off from you. Keep far from the multitude of words that are not deeds, for there is no profit in them. Do not trust words without deeds, because they are despised in the justice of God. Do not sleep at harvest time, so that you do not wear rags on the day of recompense. Trample the desire of your body, so that the Adversary may not be exalted over you as before. Send wine to the sick, and let it not be a beloved companion to you, lest your secrets be revealed in a place full of passions. Do not give rest to your desires, for at all times they conceive iniquity. Do not open doors to bodily pleasures, lest your city be overrun and the Adversary take you captive. Do not be [bold?] in words while you are bare of deeds, lest you be found guilty

at the wedding feast because you have no garments. Sow good seed for yourself in fruitful lands, so that you do not [lament?] in a place where no one helps the needy. Prepare your lamp, full of the oil of compassion and love, so that your light does not go out among [those] wrapped in light. Look for death at all times, and ask for mercy while you are alive, so that the Judge does not grow angry with you and you go and fall into the prison house. Flee from the bodily love of the daughters of Eve, and do not linger, for mighty men have perished in its net. Do not let your gaze stray beyond the bounds of chastity, lest the Adversary [wound?] you through your senses and cast you down from your covenant. Do not let your mind wander outside the way of the cross, lest thieves gain strength against you and take your treasures from you. Do not be [?] on the road that goes to Jericho and leave the road to Jerusalem, lest robbers strip you and your wounds are never healed again.

By Mar Abraham. Teaching for the brothers.

Walk in the way of peace, for it is the new commandment of the voice of the [Living One?]. Set the truth of faith within your heart, for it is the way of life that brings you up to heaven. Build yourself a tower of good works, by which you will reach the place where [comforts] dwell and abound [?]. Lay up for yourself a good treasure and the wealth of love, by which you will put on glorious garments of light [?] and a robe of incorruption. Lay up for yourself [a treasure] of virtue in the heavenly storehouses, and [thieves?] will not plunder your spiritual merchandise. Keep in your mind the commandments of [?] in the hope of [?]; and see, you do not fear [?] of the judgment [?]. Walk victoriously, carrying his yoke in the gentleness of Christ, and the fire of Gehenna will have no power over you on the day of the recompense of works. Do not be anxious about the body's [?] [satiety?] and drunkenness. Let your soul and your body belong to our Lord, and he will supply your needs for this short time. It is not fitting for us to mix with [the world?] and with mammon, for they are [opposed?] to each other. Rather, just as we have died in the mystery of baptism [?] to the whole way of life [of the world?], let us bring the fear of God to perfection in deeds, like [?]

[good]. Let conduct shine like the sun, and let the mind be [humble], and [with ...] let us do works pleasing to God, and ask for mercy in words as sinners. For if the humility of suffering and the tears of discernment do not [prevail] over the inner freedom of man — through the remembrance of former deeds and the weakness of nature, and the fact that a person sins many times without noticing — [?] let the person repent. So let no one's mind be exalted by wonders, for they are not victories; rather it is his goodness [?] that the Son of the Living One determines [?]. When we fall, in our stumblings he is victorious [?]. He has mercy as a just Judge, who forgives the debts of penitents when they knock at his door. Let us not walk on the road on which many walk and go down to the place of darkness, but let us walk on the road that, though narrow at its beginning, brings gladness at its end. Let us not build ourselves a house whose foundations are uprooted and whose beauties perish, but let us pitch for ourselves tabernacles out of conduct pleasing to God, in which even the hired laborers who come to the door of the Living One are received and rejoice with us in the place of glory. Acquire for yourself a gentle walk, a quiet voice, pleasant speech, [?] teaching, a modest look, a lowered gaze, measured laughter, a humble [garment], simple food, perfect love, [reading] of the Scriptures, the singing of psalms with the discernment of [?], and care for purity of thought. These befit those who [withdraw?] from the world and dwell in solitude. Let no place be given [to ...], nor [?] clothing. There is [?] ... slanderers. In temptation to strike [?], and in ignorance [?] again to listen [?]. To make a good report known, gracefully, even if it is said about someone who does not possess the quality — not for his sake, but for the sake of [the good] itself, which is beautiful and worthy. But to hate an evil report with all one's strength, and not to incline the ear to it lightly, even if it is true; so that we do not imagine that we look into the [faults?] of others. [For] we are judges of ourselves. And let anger not seize [us] against

our adversaries, for there is One who judges and also requites. Let us not offer our offering on the altar while our heart holds a grudge against anyone. For our Lord's justice does not want this: that his commandment should be broken while we receive forgiveness. For thus he said: "Should you not have had mercy on your fellow servant, as I had mercy on you?" Let us seek reconciliation with those who anger us; before [they ...], let them seek forgiveness from us. For if that Righteous One asked mercy for his crucifiers, how much more ought we sinners to do [this], since we are debtors in everything. Let us not keep resentment in our heart; even if it grows strong against us, let it quickly depart from us. Just as no one can swallow deadly poison for a moment without its destroying him, so too anger cannot remain in the soul without doing harm. [Nothing of the] world is fitting [?] for you, nor in the world [?]. Let [?] not be disturbed by insult, nor [?] by praises. Who is [free?] from temporal life, seeing how entangled it is in one of these? Do not count on, in your mind, a day you have not yet seen, for it is not known whether you will be alive on it or not.

By Mar Abraham. [?] and admonition and warnings, with the temptations, to the solitary brothers.

For the Adversary, my beloved, is skilled, and [?] against us [?], and against the strong and the victorious he prepares [?]. [?] for they are [far?] from him, and he does not approach. With the path [?] he takes [?]. So the children of light do not fear him, for darkness flees from anything of light. If he [attacks] them [with ...], they overcome him by fasting, after the likeness of our Savior. If he fights with them through the desire of the [eyes?], they lift their eyes to the [heights] of heaven. If he wishes to trouble them with persuasion, they do not give him a hearing. If he wishes to fight with them openly [?], they are already clothed in [armor?] and stand to meet him. If he wishes to come upon them in sleep, they wake up and overcome him. If he tempts them with possessions, they give them to the needy. If he comes upon them like something sweet, they do not taste him, for they know that he is bitter. If he inflames them with the desire for Eve, they live by themselves and not with the daughters of Eve. My beloved brothers, the door

…is open. The road is level, and the spring flows and gives drink to the thirsty. The table is prepared. The banquet is ready. The fatted ox is [?]. The cup of salvation is mixed and the perfume is made ready. The bridegroom is near to recline at table. The messengers have issued the invitation, and the guests have made ready; many [?]. Chosen ones, prepare yourselves! The light has dawned, exalted and beautiful. Garments not made by hands are prepared. The trumpet is near. The graves are opened. Treasures are revealed. The dead rise, and the living fly up in haste to meet the King. The [?] is set out. The lamps are kindled. The trumpets sound. The Watchers of heaven run. The throne is set for judgment. He who has labored rejoices, and he who has acted wickedly does not [?] judgment. Those of the right hand rejoice, and those of the left weep and wail. Then they repent [?], and those in darkness lament [?]. They beg that their tongue be moistened, and there is no one to answer them. Grace has passed away, and justice reigns. There is no repentance in that place. Winter has drawn near, and the summer of labor has passed. The Sabbath of rest is coming. The world comes to an end, and night ceases. Light reigns. Death is broken, and lamentation [?] remains. Those who go to Sheol weep and gnash their teeth. Those who go to the Kingdom see, dance, rejoice and give praise. Those who did not take wives are served by the Watchers of heaven. So set your heart diligently, my beloved, on what I am telling you: as cold water is to a thirsty soul, so are the words of the Spirit to a good soul. As the rising of the sun is to the eyes [?], so is the thought of God to a diligent soul. As a house full of good treasures, so is the man who is rich in good works. As a lamp that lights the whole house, so is the knowledge of God to a zealous [?] soul. As an adorned dwelling arranged with wisdom, so is the one who adorns himself by keeping the life-giving commandments of our Savior. As good earth crowned with its fruits and flowers, so is the man who speaks with patience. By my lord Abraham [?]: commandments and exact admonitions for one who loves good things. Before all else, it is fitting for the one who has taken the yoke of Christ upon himself that his faith be true, that he be diligent in fasting and prayer, fervent in the love of Christ, humble, gentle [?] and obedient, and that his speech be mild

and calm. Let his manner be agreeable toward all [?]. Let him speak his words with measure [?], and set a fence about his mouth against harmful words. Let him keep boisterous laughter far from him. Let him not love the adornment of garments; nor let his hair [?]; nor is it fitting for him to anoint himself with fragrant ointments. Let him not be sustained by drinking; nor is it right for him to wear soft garments, nor to ride [?] on donkeys. Let him keep the [?] eye far from him; nor is it fitting for him to look upon [?]. Let him put away from him a deceitful tongue, and let folly [?] and strife depart from him. Let him cast away from him lips of deceit. Words spoken against a person when the one they concern is not present, let him neither listen to nor look into. Mockery is a hateful death, and to bring up charges over nothing is not fitting. Let him not lend and take interest. Let him not love greed. Let him be overcome and not overcome [?]. Let him keep disorder far from him. Let him not speak jesting words. Let him not mock a man who repents of his sins, nor deride his brother who fasts, nor shame one who cannot fast. Where he is received, let him stay [?]; and where they do not receive him, let him [?] himself. Let him speak his word at an acceptable time; if not, let him keep silent. For the sake of his belly let him not demean himself by begging. To one who fears God let him reveal his secret. Let him guard against evil. Let him say nothing evil about anyone behind his back, nor [?]. Let him so conduct himself that he has no enemy at all. When people envy him for some good, let him add to his good deeds. Let him not be distressed over his loss [?]. When he has something and gives to the poor, let him rejoice; when he has nothing, let it not grieve him. Let him not keep company with an evil man. Let him not speak with an abusive man, lest he give himself over to abuse. Let him not [?] with a blasphemer, lest blasphemy come about on his account. Let him keep far from slander, and let him not flatter anyone with fine words. These things befit the solitaries [?], who receive the yoke of Christ and become penitents. And so it befits them to be like their Lord, who, though rich, made himself poor; though exalted, humbled himself; and though heaven and earth are his, had nowhere

to lay his head. Awaken yourself, my beloved, my soul! Virginity is beloved, the heavenly portion, the purity that is with [the Watchers?] on high; for nothing compares with it. Christ dwells in those who are such. The time of summer has drawn near. The fig tree has blossomed and put forth its leaves. The signs our Savior gave are beginning to be fulfilled. For he said: “Nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines, earthquakes and plagues in various places.” And behold, all these things are being fulfilled in our days. O virgins who have betrothed yourselves to Christ: when one of the sons of the covenant says to one of [the daughters of the covenant?], “Live with me and serve me,” let her answer him thus: “I am betrothed to a royal man, and it is him I serve. My betrothed will be angry with me, write me a bill of divorce and send me out of his house. And you will be grieved [?] when you are separated from me and I from you. Shame will come upon me and you. Do not put fire in your bosom and burn your garments. Rather, keep to your honor alone, and I alone to mine. Prepare your lamps [?] for the King's wedding feast, and I will prepare oil for him, so that I may go in with the wise virgins and not be shut out with the foolish.” I subdue my body and enslave it, as Paul said, lest, after preaching to others, I myself be rejected. I make my body a slave; I enslave it and subdue it. I do not give it what it wants, to be clothed [?] and to take its ease, nor do I let it be honored as it wishes, but rather I keep it in labor and weariness, in vigils and nakedness [?], in much fasting, in prayers, in supplications and in wailing [?], in many bitter tears, in humility for the sake of our Lord, in patience and long-suffering of spirit. I subject myself, so that like a slave it may honor everyone, standing up before everyone. I make it run on its feet like a slave, and conciliate its adversaries, so that it may not be made to stumble by them [?], and bow its head before one lesser than itself, as our Lord bowed his head and was baptized by John, who was his servant and his creature, to be a teacher for us, that we too should do the same toward one lesser than ourselves. I make it wash the feet of its adversaries and greet in peace those who hate it [?]. I make it call [others] its brothers and sisters, my sons and daughters [?], my lords and my fathers, just as that good Lord called his servants

brothers, and called his betrayer “friend.” If he called his betrayer “friend,” how much more those who love him! I lead it wherever it does not wish to go, to its enemies who do not perceive it [?], to serve the servants of servants like the slave of all, just as our Lord served the wicked and those who crucified him. And I do these things so that sin may not sink me; for behold, it wars against people from without and from within, sin and those of its kind. Struggle, my beloved brothers, for the fruits have come and ripened, and behold, they are being gathered into the storehouse of eternal life. My beloved, the time is now short [?], and no one can care for his own soul so long as he cares for the world. And just as no one can look at heaven with one eye and at the earth with the other, so the mind cannot care for God and for the world. Fear God, as one who is about to give account of his deeds. For just as the earth cannot yield fruit without seed, so a person cannot repent without humility. Let him take care to guard himself even against small slips [?]. Whoever loves God, there is nothing in the world that can separate him from him. For it is written: “Who will separate me from the love of Christ? Hunger, or distress?” and the rest. Again, on the snares and traps of Satan, and on purity and the perfection of righteousness, by my lord Abraham. For [?] from the world in the name of [?], and when they have come into the midst, he sets his bow with [?] stumbling blocks. They fall and are caught in the traps of perdition. Flee from the counsel of the deceiver, who hands out stumbling blocks to merchants. For he is crafty: first he casts food on his trap for the prey, and his love [?] goes before his food. Like Judas, he kisses and kills. If you let him stand [?], he will repay you with a fall. If you give life to the body in its mortality, it in turn becomes death to your life. Among men [?] the Just One is forbearing: he does not exact payment at the very hour one sins. For this reason repentance of soul comes, for two reasons: that if he repents, [it becomes] a cause [?] of his entering in; and if not, [?] his departure in the spirit [?]. Since for all your debts repentance of soul is near [?]

so that it may take its testimony with it to the court of judgment. Let the body learn repentance, and not [only] the remorse of soul that comes at every hour [?]. For repentance is the physician of your soul; and this is what remorse of soul gains [?]: that it [?] and [?] its pains at every hour. O youth, full of eager running, do not spend your strength [?] in the pleasure of bodily desires, which serve you [?] and consume your strength; tomorrow [?] it will leave you, so that your old age comes to shame. Run swiftly, O youth, in the contest of righteousness, so that your old age may receive the crown. For just as a pure priest can purify the temple in which he ministers, so a pure mind can purify the body from all shameful deeds and hateful thoughts and make it a pure vessel, as it is written: “fit for use, a dwelling of its Lord, prepared for every good work,” and perfect, by the grace and mercies of our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom be glory, and upon us his mercies and compassion forever. Amen and amen.

Comparisons that urge toward excellence, by my lord Abraham. As cold water is to a thirsty soul, so are the words of the Spirit to a good soul. As the rising of the sun is to [all] natures, so is the thought of God to a good soul. As a great house full of good treasures, so is the man who is rich in good works. As a lamp that lights the whole house, so is the knowledge of God in the soul. As an adorned dwelling arranged with wisdom, so is the one who adorns himself by keeping the commandments of our Savior. As good earth crowned with fruits and flowers, so is the man who speaks with patience.

Again, comparisons that apply to the lax: those who have cut off their hope and given themselves over to the service of impurity and shameful desires, whose ways are loose at all times and who love many harmful pleasures, are like barren land, a parched [?] and desolate [?] wilderness, a vineyard without fruit, an empty vessel, a body without a soul, eyes without light. Against those who love praise and act foolishly [?] in their wickedness: they are like a broken cistern, purses with holes, a tree without fruit, a naked man, a [?] vessel, wood into which rot has fallen, the remnant of garments eaten by moths. Against the one who is not

careful with his tongue: he is like one whose house doors stand open, and who is plundered [?] by everyone; like a jar of wine that is not covered; like something unsealed. Against those over whom evil thoughts rule, and wicked thoughts rise up in their hearts: they are like a dwelling of beasts, a den full of harmful and deadly reptiles, a ship tossed by the waves, a land full of forest and thorns that spring up and choke it. Against the one who does not subdue his soul: he is like a strong, untamed beast that tramples everyone [?] and roams in pleasure. Again, concerning the one who cares for his own soul and has become a cause [of good] for another: he is like a righteous [?], a light [?] that illumines the people, a wise pilot [?], a pleasant mirror [?], a shining lamp, a harbor of good things, an angel of God; like the mouth of [?], and like a great one of God. I have written these things to you in all their variety, so that you may not grow weary [?] and your soul may not grow slack, and so that it may be of benefit to those who wish to profit from you. For this reason I counsel you: since from your youth you chose to bear the good yoke of patience on the shoulder of your will, this will help you: to sit alone in quiet, kept apart from the conversation of people and from the [?] disturbances of these times. Make yourself as dust in humility toward everyone, knowing that there is a reward for your tears. Make your cell a court of judgment for yourself, and a place of struggle with wild beasts and evil passions. Let there be pictured in it Gehenna and the Kingdom, death and life, sinners and the righteous, the fire that is not quenched and the glory of the just, the outer darkness, the gnashing of teeth and the worm that does not die, the light of the righteous and the joy of the bridal chamber, the passion of our Lord and the remembrance of his resurrection, and the salvation of creation. And make it [?] for your dwelling [?], the mystery of baptism, of repentance and of the forgiveness of sins. Bathe in it evening and morning, at all hours and times: scrub, wash and cleanse the blemishes of your soul. For if a person is not born with a new birth in repentance, and does not strip off the old man with all his ways, his [?] and his desires, and put on the new conduct that follows the resurrection, he cannot enter the Kingdom of God. And let your life be kept

from excess. One of two things will happen to you: either you will be distressed when you suffer in these things, or, when you spare yourself from them, it will be increased and your pain will grow severe [?]. Beware lest, for the sake of honor and concern for guests, the Evil One cast you down in battle. Do not acquire any desire that comes from the lust of the belly [?]. The battle with the dark ones is enough for you. Bolt [?], close and guard your dwelling. These things God is pleased with, he who knows your sitting, your going in and your coming out, and all your conduct. Be constant in prayer, especially at the time of the nights, which is an acceptable time, as it is written, so that you may be like your Lord, who kept vigil in prayer to God. At the hour when all voices are silent, fill your mouth with praise and your tongue with thanksgiving. While others lie on their beds like the dead, depict in yourself the wakefulness of the resurrection. The night that is dark to others shines for you like noonday. Instead of others who are drunk at night, be drunk with the love of God. In the night when silver and gold are stolen, steal the Kingdom like a thief. In the night when sinners toil at evil deeds as their [?], you [toil] for your profit. And when morning comes, [mingle?] with everyone. With merchants work; with [?] draw near [?]; with farmers till; with shepherds tend the flock; with builders build; with runners run on the roads; with judges [judge?]; with [?] [?]; with money-changers [?] [?]; with those who forgive, forgive. Take the [gain?] of them all upon yourself. Then that Merciful One, [abundant] in his gifts and rich toward all who call on him, will quickly come to you and help you. And when you are clothed [with these], beautiful thoughts of [?] rise up in you, and your mind is strengthened, and the way before you becomes smooth, [the] rough [places] a plain, and the Lord [?] teaches you [?]. You anticipate the conduct that is to come, and you fulfill the will of God, as in heaven so on earth. And in step with your conduct your knowledge also grows, your vision becomes great, and you are made worthy of the vision of spiritual things.

Again, on the visions and revelations that come to the saints, by my lord Abraham. Since it is profitable, let us now state the causes of revelations and visions in brief:

What is the reason that some see revelations and others do not, though they are fully equal in their conduct; and some surpass their companions in labors, yet are not made worthy of the vision of spiritual things as they are? This is the first cause: the cause of revelations is the faith of the soul. And because faith does not belong to everyone, not everyone sees revelations. The second cause is this: because need demands it, as the ancients often saw because there was need, not only the excellent but also the wicked, like Balaam the diviner and the Magi, together with others. The third cause is the encouragement of the weak, as with Jacob when he feared Esau, and as with Stephen and his companions at the time of their contests. The fourth cause is the wakefulness and diligence of a person over himself. For just as springs, when their waters are stirred up with much [mud?], become murky, but when they settle [?] become clear and bright, so when people weigh down their hearts with gluttony, drunkenness and much eating, their minds are darkened and they cannot see divine visions, since their body is sunk in the heaviness of sleep. But those who strip themselves of all these things, because their body is light, are awake to the movements of their soul and shine like bright springs; they are made worthy of revelations. The fifth cause is [?] meditation: because the mind meditates continually on [God?], on the angels, on the light in which is salvation, and on [?] in which the righteous will inherit, they are made worthy in return [?] to delight in the vision as [?] in their soul. Purity of soul and purity of heart make a person [see God], according to the word of our Lord. The sixth cause is humility: that a person does not reckon himself as anything in his own eyes; and because he humbles himself, his Lord exalts him in excellence and in revelations, and he is not puffed up. But those who trust in themselves that they are righteous, if they see a revelation, see it to the destruction of their labors, and it becomes their fall. Since these are the causes of the visions shown by God, do not be puffed up if you see anything. I want to teach you how to distinguish true visions from false ones, and those of God from those of Satan. For when the revelation

a person sees is of God or of angels, at that very hour he is filled with joy and moved to praise. His body grows warm and his face flushes; he burns with love and gains tranquility [?]; his mind is made firm [?] in faith, and a pleasant fragrance is smelled. But in a false vision, which comes from the Evil One, at that very hour the soul is troubled and shaken and falls into fear. The person's color turns pale, and his tongue cleaves to the roof of his mouth, like someone whom another is seeking to kill, and the hairs of his head stand on end. Other such things it was not permitted to us to write about true visions, nor do we write about false ones. For it is fitting for us to conceal some things from our adversaries, so that the word of Scripture may not be fulfilled against us, which says: “He who reveals a secret destroys [?] his own soul.” Concerning such things, let us ask wisdom from above, and it will be given to us. And what we have left out you can find in the writings of the fathers. But here I complete this treatise and bring it to an end, urging you, who have been the occasion for my writing such things, and all who share your mind, to include a prayer for me in your prayers, that I may not sit in darkness like the dead of old, and that that [day?] of your [?] may not find me unprepared [?] while I am sunk in the heavy sleep of negligence. Rather, let us implore the grace of him who came into the world to give life to sinners and to grant forgiveness of their sins; to him be praise and exaltation, and upon us his mercies and compassion forever. Amen.

Here ends the writing of the whole treatise of Mar Abraham.

Next, the histories of the holy fathers who [?] will be set out, for the confirmation of [?], collected and set down for the excellence [?] and love of God [?], by [?] Bar Hadbshabba, priest and head of the [?] of the holy [?] of the city of Nisibis, [?] in spirit. Although I was hindered by many things in this zeal to collect the histories of the holy fathers and to show the purity of their [?]: first by ignorance, second by youth, third by [?], and greater than all these, by the evil times which [?] trouble the mind and [?] draw it away from learning; yet the love and affection for the deeds of the fathers, and the purity of their excellence, prevailed over all these.
